world_news.headline: Dozens arrested after fatal pre-dawn shootout in Dutch village
world_news.summary:
Police urged people in Overasselt to stay indoors after one person died and 34 were arrested

Authorities have arrested 34 people, including French, Belgian and Algerian nationals, after a person died in a pre-dawn shootout in a Dutch village reportedly linked to a notorious drug lord.

Police urged people in Overasselt, near the German border, to stay indoors with doors and windows shut in case further suspects were on the loose.

world_news.headline: News live: Five Australians confirmed safe after Nepal-Tibet flooding; Chanel Contos urges action on ‘manosphere’
world_news.summary:
Package steps up support to fight transnational drug trafficking flowing through the Pacific. Follow the day’s news live

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

‘Great news’ that five Australians found safe in Nepal amid grave concerns for those still missing

The minister for the defence industry, Pat Conroy, said the revelation that five Australians have been confirmed safe in Nepal since yesterday morning is “great news”, but said the government still had grave concerns for the 38 others still unaccounted for.

Obviously having five citizens confirmed safe, which is great news for those Australians and their families, reduces the numbers of unaccounted Australians down to 38.

But we are very concerned for the safety of those 38 that have not had contact with their families or next to kin since the disaster struck. And we’re really focused on establishing their whereabouts and supporting their families in this very difficult time and supporting the people of Nepal in what is tragic circumstances.

world_news.headline: US launches new airstrikes on Iranian targets as hostilities flare
world_news.summary:
Move from Washington quashes hopes that exchange of fire last weekend might not presage ⁠wider renewal of hostilities

The US launched new airstrikes on Iranian targets on Tuesday, quashing hopes that an exchange of fire last ⁠weekend might not presage a ⁠wider renewal of hostilities.

Oil prices had ​already risen after that first exchange of direct attacks since July and after reports of two tankers being hit leaving the strait of Hormuz, the global oil supply waterway that Iran has effectively closed to shipping.

world_news.headline: Relief as Australians missing in Nepal-Tibet flood disaster found alive
world_news.summary:
Five missing Australians have been found since Tuesday morning, bringing the total citizens unaccounted for to 38

  • Australians missing in the Nepal floods: what we know so far

A total of five Australians missing after devastating floods ravaged the Nepal-Tibet border last week have been found.

Of the five Australians confirmed safe, one was found in Nepal, one in Tibet, one in China and three outside the crisis-hit area. The total number still missing is 38.
